chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The dung-eating she-camel: do not eat its meat, nor drink its milk, until it is fed for forty days; and the dung-eating cow: do not eat its meat, nor drink its milk, until it is fed for thirty days; and the dung-eating sheep: do not eat its meat, nor drink its milk, until it is fed for ten days; and the dung-eating duck: do not eat its meat until it is restrained for five days; and the chicken for three days.'

key_terms.الْجَلَّالَةُ: An animal that eats waste or dung; its meat and milk are considered impure until purified by feeding.
key_terms.تُرْبَطَ: It is restrained/confined (specifically for poultry to prevent them from eating waste).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat and milk from dung-eating animals (Jallalah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the fiqh of 'Jallalah' (animals feeding on impurities), establishing a purification period where they are fed clean fodder to ensure their meat and milk are Halal. The varying durations—40 days for camels, 30 for cows, 10 for sheep, and shorter periods for poultry—reflect the scholarly understanding of metabolic clearance rates in different species, a ruling widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence to maintain ritual purity.
